text: Angal Enen is a stable indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.

text: South Angal, also known as Angal Enen, Nembi, Magi (Megi) or South Mendi, is spoken by anywhere from 12,000 to 22,000 people (1982) living in the Nembi Valley and on the Nembi Plateau in the central portion of Papua New Guinea's Southern Highlands Province.
